claims.statement: `create_deep_agent` separates declarative and compiled synchronous subagents from `AsyncSubAgent` specs, adds a default synchronous `general-purpose` worker unless the harness profile disables or replaces it, and installs the synchronous `task` middleware and asynchronous task middleware independently.

A synchronous declarative subagent is isolated by default: it receives a new task message and state with messages, todos, structured response, skill metadata, pinned skills, disclosure metadata, fork marker, and private fields excluded; explicit child permissions or `interrupt_on` replace inherited values, while omitted values inherit the parent configuration.

Experimental `mode="fork"` reconstructs the parent's effective history and prompt context for a delegated task but forbids an independent skills list and refuses nested `task` calls, preventing recursive delegation.

The synchronous task boundary returns one ToolMessage for the original tool call: it serializes a non-null child `structured_response` as JSON or otherwise forwards the last non-empty child AI message, while excluding child-only and private state fields from parent updates.

Async subagents launch Agent Protocol runs in remote threads and persist task metadata in `async_tasks`; dedicated tools then check results, replace a running task's run on update, cancel it, or list refreshed status, while URL-less ASGI transport requires an async parent invocation.

`SkillsMiddleware` discovers `SKILL.md` metadata through backend APIs, overlays same-named skills by source order, caches the resulting index in `skills_metadata` until it is set to `None`, and injects a progressive-disclosure prompt that directs the model to read full instructions on demand.

Top-level skills are applied to the main graph and its auto-generated general-purpose worker; named isolated declarative subagents receive skills only from their own `skills` spec, while forked subagents replay the parent's skill behavior and cannot specify separate sources.

The synchronous `task` interface accepts only `description` and `subagent_type` (apart from injected runtime), rejects duplicate subagent names and invalid modes before execution, and retains `handoff` as an alias for isolated mode.
Synchronous subagent invocation preserves ambient parent configuration while marking the LangSmith tracing context and child configurable metadata with `ls_agent_type="subagent"`.

Skill loading records source-level failures in `skills_load_errors`; prompt rendering bounds and escapes those diagnostics and labels them as untrusted, while `system_prompt=None` suppresses only the prompt fragment and not metadata loading.

Skill-selected tools are not registered in the ordinary tool node; a successful `read_file` result for a known skill's `SKILL.md` or a pinned-skill message resolves `metadata.include_tools` for a subsequent model call, and records only gated tools in `_skill_tools_disclosed`.

At execution time, `SkillsMiddleware` admits an otherwise unregistered skill tool only when the latest disclosure record maps its name to an include name and the resolver still returns it; unrecorded, same-turn, or stale-resolution calls remain invalid-tool errors.

Skill tool disclosure uses provider-specific request formats: supported Anthropic models receive inline `tool_addition` blocks and supported OpenAI Responses models receive `additional_tools` items anchored after the read's tool-result batch; other models receive tools bound on the request, while the disclosure record preserves the same execution gate.
When a skill read or pinned skill is removed by compaction, its skill tools are withdrawn unless another remaining trigger produces them, in which case disclosure is re-anchored to that trigger.

`pinned_skills` supplies a one-turn, full-instruction snapshot: before the next model call the middleware resolves known names in first-seen order, appends readable `SKILL.md` bodies without frontmatter as attributed `HumanMessage` entries, and clears the request with `Overwrite([])`.

A pinned skill remains a conversation snapshot after its source changes; pinning it again reads and appends the current content, while subagent return-state filtering prevents a child from pinning skills into its parent.
